awd_titl_txt: CRII: OAC: High-Efficiency Serverless Computing Systems for Deep Learning: A Hybrid CPU/GPU Architecture
awd_abstract_narration:
This award is funded in whole or in part under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Public Law 117-2).

Next-generation serverless cloud computing provides developers with simplified access to server management and administration, including event-driven execution, fine-grained resource provisioning, auto-scaling, and pay-as-you-go billing. The machine learning community is taking advantage of these benefits of serverless cloud computing to ease the development and deployment of deep learning (DL) applications. However, existing serverless computing platforms lack efficient support for  GPUs, impeding DL practitioners from utilizing serverless computing for large-scale applications. This project will develop an efficient serverless computing platform with a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture to accelerate DL application development and deployment. The goal is to advance cutting-edge methodologies in both deep learning and serverless computing, which will result in a significant leap forward to benefit DL practitioners, DL users, and providers of cloud computing infrastructures, contributing to science advancement for society. The research findings will also enhance undergraduate and graduate education with exciting examples and demonstrations of real-world systems at the intersection of distributed computing, cloud computing, and deep learning.

The project will develop a novel serverless computing platform with a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture that will provide DL applications with native GPU performance. Two core components constitute the hybrid serverless computing architecture, a shim virtualized GPU (vGPU) layer and a refactored container subsystem. The shim vGPU layer enables high-performance GPU sharing for concurrent serverless functions with low latency and high scalability. This layer provides fine-grained GPU resource provisioning and performance isolation by intercepting GPU calls from serverless functions using API remoting techniques. The vGPU layer optimizes GPU performance in serverless computing via GPU context caching and locality-aware scheduling to mitigate cold-starts and unnecessary data movement. The container subsystem accelerates the entire DL lifecycle by exploiting DL model structures and pipelined model loading to parallelize CPU-to-GPU memory copy and model execution. The subsystem exploits model partitioning techniques to accelerate the hybrid CPU/GPU architecture by dynamically distributing the DL model partitions to CPU and GPU. The scientific knowledge and tools designed and implemented from this research project will provide and enable innovations for next-generation cloud computing and deep learning.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project developed and evaluated new ways to run deep learning workloads efficiently on "serverless" computing platforms---systems that automatically scale resources up and down and charge only for what is used. While serverless computing is widely used for lightweight web services, it has historically been difficult to use for deep learning because training and serving models often require GPUs, large memory footprints, and fast access to model data. The central goal of this award was to make serverless computing practical and energy/cost-efficient for deep learning by designing a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture and system techniques that reduce end-to-end latency and improve resource utilization.


Over the life of the award, our work produced system designs, prototypes, and experimental evidence showing that serverless platforms can support more demanding machine learning workloads than previously possible. One major outcome was enabling reinforcement learning (RL)---a form of machine learning used in robotics, recommendation, and decision-making---on serverless infrastructure. We demonstrated how serverless can be used not only for single-agent RL, but also for multi-agent RL, where many learning agents interact and train in parallel. This expands the range of AI training problems that can benefit from the elasticity and pay-as-you-go model of serverless computing, while reducing the operational complexity typically required to manage large clusters.


A second major outcome addressed a key barrier in serverless deep learning: inference latency caused by "cold-path" overheads such as loading models and initializing runtimes when functions are invoked. We developed techniques such as opportunistic pre-loading that proactively prepare frequently used model components on serverless clusters, significantly reducing response time without sacrificing the flexibility of serverless scaling. These ideas help make serverless more suitable for real-time AI services where users expect fast, consistent responses.


A third outcome advanced hybrid CPU/GPU approaches for emerging large-model serving. Modern large language models and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can require substantial GPU memory, making them expensive to serve at low latency. We explored fine-grained offloading strategies that move selected model components between GPU and other resources to balance memory usage and speed. This work helps clarify the trade-offs and system mechanisms needed to serve increasingly large AI models efficiently.


The broader impacts of the project include workforce development and open dissemination. The award supported hands-on training for students through building and evaluating real systems, and it contributed to outreach activities that engaged learners at multiple levels. Research results were shared through peer-reviewed publications and public artifacts, helping other researchers and practitioners adopt and build upon the techniques. Overall, the project advances the intellectual merit of computer systems and AI infrastructure by expanding what serverless platforms can do for deep learning, and it supports broader societal benefits by lowering barriers to scalable, efficient AI computing.
